authors: Rie Roselyne Yotsu et al. (Tulane University)

relevance: Trains ResNet-50 and VGG-16 convolutional neural networks on 1,709 clinical photographs from 506 patients collected prospectively in Cote d'Ivoire and Ghana to diagnose five skin neglected tropical diseases (Buruli ulcer, leprosy, mycetoma, scabies, yaws). The two models correctly predicted over 70% of diagnoses, ResNet-50 outperformed VGG-16, and performance improved consistently with training size; training on PCR-confirmed Buruli ulcer cases added 1-3% accuracy. The authors stress the explicit focus on dark skin, which they note is under-represented in dermatology AI datasets.
